from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors are not just arrows in space.",
            "They are objects obeying specific algebraic rules.",
            "Think of functions as vectors, not arrows.",
            "We define spaces by rules, not shapes.",
            "Abstraction lets us solve wider classes of problems."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Bridge: From Geometry to Abstraction", lecture_lines)
        
        # Objects
        arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5 + UP*1.0, color=BLUE)
        func_curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[-1.2, 1.2], color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        axioms = MathTex(r"u+v = v+u", r"c(u+v) = cu+cv", font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(axioms, "D5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(axioms))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow))
        self.place_in_area(func_curve, "B4", "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(func_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(RED))
        rule_box = SurroundingRectangle(axioms, color=RED, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(rule_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Defining the 'Rules of the Game'", 
            ["Closure ensures operations stay within the set.", 
             "Adding two vectors must yield another vector.", 
             "Scaling a vector must also remain inside."]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show set V (color #FFFFFF) containing vectors (color #FF5733)
        set_v = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(set_v, 'C3')
        v1 = Dot(color="#FF5733").move_to(self.grid['B2'])
        v2 = Dot(color="#FF5733").move_to(self.grid['D4'])
        self.play(Create(set_v), FadeIn(v1), FadeIn(v2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show vector addition: v + w = u (all color #33FF57)
        v_label = MathTex("v", color="#33FF57").next_to(v1, UP, buff=0.1)
        w_label = MathTex("w", color="#33FF57").next_to(v2, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        vec1 = Arrow(start=self.grid['C3'], end=v1.get_center(), color="#33FF57", buff=0)
        vec2 = Arrow(start=self.grid['C3'], end=v2.get_center(), color="#33FF57", buff=0)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(v_label), FadeIn(w_label), 
            Create(vec1), Create(vec2),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57")
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show scalar multiplication: c * v = w (all color #3357FF)
        c_val = MathTex("c", color="#3357FF").move_to(self.grid['E2'])
        scaled_vec = Arrow(start=self.grid['C3'], end=self.grid['E5'], color="#3357FF", buff=0)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(c_val), Create(scaled_vec),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3357FF")
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Diverse Examples: Functions as Vectors", [
            "Polynomials can behave just like standard vectors.",
            "Function spaces follow the same linear rules.",
            "Traits evolve within a defined vector space."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show polynomial p(x) = ax^2 + bx + c
        poly_formula = MathTex("p(x) = ax^2 + bx + c", color="#F1C40F")
        self.place_at_grid(poly_formula, "B2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(poly_formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#F1C40F")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show two functions f and g added together
        sum_formula = MathTex("f(x) + g(x) = h(x)", color="#9B59B6")
        self.place_at_grid(sum_formula, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(sum_formula))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#9B59B6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight common traits in a list
        traits = VGroup(
            Text("Trait A", color="#1ABC9C"),
            Text("Trait B", color="#1ABC9C"),
            Text("Trait C", color="#1ABC9C")
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_in_area(traits, "E1", "F3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(traits))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#1ABC9C")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", [
            "Vector spaces are sets with algebraic structure.",
            "Arrows, matrices, and functions are all examples.",
            "Abstraction unifies diverse mathematical concepts."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'Vector Space' at center
        vs_text = Text("Vector Space", font_size=40, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(vs_text, "B2", "E5")
        self.play(Write(vs_text))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Populate space with arrows, matrices, functions
        arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#E74C3C")
        matrix = MathTex(r"\\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\\\ c & d \\end{pmatrix}", color="#3498DB")
        func = MathTex(r"f(x) = x^2", color="#2ECC71")
        
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(func, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(arrow), FadeIn(matrix), FadeIn(func))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#E74C3C")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Flash the 'Abstraction' concept
        abs_text = Text("Abstraction", font_size=48, color="#F39C12")
        self.place_in_area(abs_text, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(FadeOut(vs_text), FadeOut(arrow), FadeOut(matrix), FadeOut(func))
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(abs_text))
        self.play(abs_text.animate.set_color(WHITE), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#F39C12")
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Abstract Vector Spaces: Beyond Arrows and Coordinates

sections.title: The Bridge: From Geometry to Abstraction (1 min)
sections.content: Transition from Euclidean vectors (arrows in 2D/3D space) to abstract vectors. Define a vector space not by 'what it looks like' (arrows), but by 'how it behaves' (the 8 axioms of addition and scalar multiplication).
sections.example: Visualizing a 'vector' as a simple arrow shifting from (0,0) to (3,2) vs. a vector that is actually a complex function, like f(x) = x².

sections.title: Defining the 'Rules of the Game' (1.5 min)
sections.content: Introduce the core requirements: Closure under addition and scalar multiplication. Use a graphical checklist animation where any set that breaks these rules is 'crossed out' and rejected from being a vector space.
sections.example: Scenario: A 'Robot Factory' where the robots (vectors) must always be able to combine (add) and be scaled (multiplied) to remain valid robots. If combining two robots creates a 'glitch' (leaves the set), the set fails the closure test.

sections.title: Diverse Examples: Functions as Vectors (1.5 min)
sections.content: Demonstrate that vectors are just 'elements' that obey the rules. Show that polynomials of degree ≤ 2 form a vector space. Visualize this by treating a parabola as a single point in a higher-dimensional 'function space'.
sections.example: Imagine a 'Digital Pet' evolution. A pet is defined by its traits. Adding two pets (traits) results in a new, valid pet within the same species-space. This shows how mathematical abstraction mirrors biological variation.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis (1 min)
sections.content: Recap: An abstract vector space is a container of objects where we can perform linear combinations. Reiterate that the 'arrows' were just a specific, intuitive realization of a much broader, powerful algebraic concept.
sections.example: Final Animation: A zoom-out view showing that arrows, matrices, and functions are all just different 'shapes' living inside the same 'Vector Space' skyscraper.
